newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids little changed, helped by crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids little changed, helped by crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices again held relatively steady Friday in stagnant, late trade, still supported by stable-to-firmer crude and the recent minor heat wave in the Northeast, market sources said.

"We're just starting to see summer, so I don't see a whole lot more downside, but East Coast demand is still not good," said one cash trader, adding he expected the spread between low and high sulphur grades in the U.S. Gulf to narrow.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $16.00 a barrel, with July one percent paper talked a quarter lower at $15.75, traders said.
While more moderate temperatures are expected in the Northeast next week, traders said expectations for hotter weather in the Southeast and Texas could temper the bears.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also notionally was unchanged at about $16.75.
High sulphurs in New York eased slightly, with 2.2 percent now talked in the $14.50-75 area, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with three percent still quoted at about $14.50 and one percent at about $16.00.
Traders said 45,000 barrels of prompt three percent sold late Thursday at $14.50 (FOB Louisiana).

New York city gate weekend gas prices held relatively steady Friday in the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.99 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also was unchanged at about $2.14/mmBtu, or $13.48 a barrel.
